brief.situation: 15:20 in an outpatient neurologic clinic. You are the physical therapist. Ms. Duvall, 54, is in gait training after an ischemic stroke 4 months ago; she also has a known unruptured cerebral aneurysm being watched by neurosurgery.
handover: Halfway down the parallel bars she stops, grabs the back of her head and says, 'That's the worst headache I've ever had. It came on like a thunderclap.'
Her blood pressure at the start of the session was 138/84.
Clinic policy: a sudden severe headache or new neurologic signs during a session: stop, stay with the patient, call 911, and tell the referring neurologist.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What do you suspect, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: A sudden, severe, worst-ever occipital headache with stiff neck, nausea and drowsiness in a person with a known aneurysm suggests aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, an emergency.
parts.modelAnswer: That sounds like her aneurysm has bled: a thunderclap, worst-ever headache at the back of her head, a stiff neck, nausea and drowsiness.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Stops, lies her down with head and shoulders raised, stays with her, checks neuro signs and blood pressure, calls 911 and the neurologist.
parts.modelAnswer: Stop, lie her down with her head up, stay with her, check her neuro and pressure, call 911, then her neurologist.

scoring.modelReasoning: Subarachnoid hemorrhage presents with a severe headache that starts suddenly, often at the back of the head and described as the worst ever, with stiff neck, nausea and vomiting, and decreased alertness; causes include a ruptured cerebral aneurysm or an arteriovenous malformation. It is an emergency: stop, stay with her, check neuro signs and blood pressure, and call 911.
